essay.title: Cent #1867
essay.subtitle: Inscription #66001799
essay.author: shibboleth
essay.version: v1 (2026-11-26): script v0.8 approved by shibboleth ('Please make the video', 00:45Z); eee take 2

_what: Cent #1867 (1964, no mint mark): Significant Obsidian, Significant Verdigris, Contaminated (Alien Secretion). Baseline format: concept C02 (metal and stamp) from the baseline text, quotes first (Chang 2017, Groys 2016), then the traits on this Cent, then value set again.

shots.purpose: Look C opening (PR #25 v3.1, title below): play button, CENTS STORY TIME, the 'look closer' sticker (approved 2026-11-25), one 3DCENTS turn, settled at frame 184 (6.13 s) before 'Every' at 6.9 s. No year or mint-mark zoom.
Concept C02 in Look C, named as the script names it: the concept takes the name's place under the coin the opening ends on. Pair: this Cent, and the two things every coin joins. True.

The same coin, now with its name again; a chip for each half as it is said. Pair: this copper cent's face is one cent and its metal is copper. True (a 1964 cent, 95% copper). No metal price on screen: the only figure is Chang's, in his quote.

Media library C063: pennies laid out on a desk at Chang's studio, with rolls, a scale and a box marked COPPER. Pair: these are such coins, hoarded at Chang's studio. True (Chang collected the copper cents that became CENTS).

Chang's own words, lit word by word (check_quotes.py FOUND in The Creative Independent, 7 July 2017; control '1.8 cents' MISSING). The card is up 0.5 s (the 'seventeen,' hold) before 'was like buying'. Starts after the sentence about melting being illegal, as approved.

quote.text: buying 1.7 cents of copper for one cent and it’s still worth one cent.

shots.purpose: Back to #1867 with its inscription line. Pair: Chang took this coin's face and metal apart. True: its obverse image is inscription 66001799, and the coin itself went into the block.

Media library C008: a grid of Cent obverse images. Pair: these images of obverses are what was inscribed. True: one image of each obverse went onto one satoshi. The image is shown, not the satoshi, the inscription or the penny.
a14, the casting (pour visible from its first frame). Pair: this is the coins being melted and cast. True (supplied by the essay's author as the casting of the block).
Media library S0718: CENTS Block Copper alone. Pair: this is the one block the coins were cast into. True. No screen and no model of CENTS Block 839969, so nothing says the block was inscribed.

Groys, lit half by half (check_quotes.py FOUND in In the Flow, Verso 2016, introduction; control 'aura without a subject' MISSING). The block lights under 'the object without an aura', the image under 'the aura without an object', as the baseline text pairs them.

quote.at_phrase: the object without an aura and the
the aura without an object. CENTS keeps

shots.purpose: The image of #1867: a slow push-in, then the zooms of 1867_zoom_plan_v0.1.jpg: O (the band over the motto and the head), V (cheek and behind the head), the collar crust, back out, then A? (Alien Secretion, Claude's reading, flagged to shibboleth). Traits read from the obverse only.
Traits Atlas, Alien Secretion, on cents.vision, the definition highlighted. Pair: this is the Atlas's definition, quoted. True.

Template #4421 (1964, no mint mark, Lustrous only), close to mint state: dissolve to it on its name, and back to #1867 (inscription line, no chip) on 'A cent held at one cent', which then carries the value line on the coin alone.

Media library C048, the MAKES CENTS interview-cover montage, under 'by the people who keep, read and exchange it'. Pair: these are people of the collection. True; an ongoing process, not a conclusion.
Closing card in Look C: one 3DCENTS turn from the first frame (150 frames), 'Cent number eighteen sixty-seven, a great Cent.' over it, then the photo until the end card.
End card, first half: the cents.gallery home page (supplied screenshot).
End card, second half: the Traits Lab on cents.vision (supplied screenshot; no wallet address).
End credits (brief §4): images, 3DCENTS, the Atlas via cents.vision, each quote's source, the cents.vision screenshots.
